installed_wheel.build_install: uv build --offline --wheel, uv venv --offline --no-project, uv pip install --offline into a new temporary environment

negative_controls.mutation: empty sitecustomize hook, ordinary MCP run completes
negative_controls.outcome: probe fails with 'MCP run returned without a server crash' in normal and optimized Python

negative_controls.mutation: replace os.kill(SIGKILL) with os._exit(17) in the MCP child hook
negative_controls.outcome: probe fails with 'MCP server did not exit with SIGKILL (17)'

negative_controls.mutation: replace the call_tool connection-close exception with an unrelated ValueError after the child dies
negative_controls.outcome: probe fails with 'reason other than connection closure'

checks.command: uv run --no-sync ruff check scripts/probe_mcp_server_crash.py tests/test_probe_ledger_commit_crash.py

independent_review: A read-only reviewer first reproduced a false positive by changing the MCP child to os._exit(17). The wrapper now waits on the installed child, ties its PID to the hook marker and requires returncode -SIGKILL. The reviewer then found no remaining false green in the stated process-crash scope; connection-close classification and three controls were checked.
limits: The wheel, case, human label, ledger and manifest are synthetic development fixtures. The test uses an installed wheel and a real stdio MCP client, but no model or human decision.

The probe covers only process death around the second ledger os.replace, before and after publication; it does not test power or host loss, filesystem durability after host failure, or every interruption point.
A successful CLI/MCP status comparison after reconnect does not establish full workflow acceptance, independent reviewer identity or source authenticity.
